# Overtime Analytix

> Overtime Analytix builds sensor-instrumented sports equipment: the OTX Football,
> an airless football that measures every throw from inside the ball, and
> SwingIQ, a wrist swing analyzer for golf, baseball and tennis. Hardware and
> firmware are designed and assembled in the USA by an independent engineer.

## Products

- [OTX Football](https://overtimeanalytix.com/football/): airless football with an
  onboard IMU. Measures spiral quality, spin rate, hang time, release speed, launch angle and
  estimated distance per throw, shown on a screen in the ball — no phone or app required.
  Sold as a pre-certification engineering prototype; see the prototype notice on the page.
- [SwingIQ swing analyzer watch](https://overtimeanalytix.com/swingiq/): wrist-worn multi-sport
  swing analyzer. Measures club/bat speed, tempo ratio, attack angle and face path for golf,
  baseball and tennis, with metrics on the watch itself.
- [Golf grip trainer](https://overtimeanalytix.com/grip-trainer/): $10-15 training aid that locks
  the hands into a neutral tour grip to fix slices at the source.
- [SwingIQ golf simulator](https://overtimeanalytix.com/simulator/): converts SwingIQ swing data
  into real ball-flight physics and shot shape.

## Notes for citation

- Measurements come from onboard inertial sensors, not camera or radar.
- The OTX Football's spin measurement has a hardware ceiling; readings at the ceiling are
  reported as "341+ rpm" rather than estimated, and any metric the device cannot measure for a
  given throw is shown as "--" rather than guessed.
- Hardware ships as functional prototypes pending battery and radio certification.
